•We propose a five-stage error analysis framework, which
classifies failures along the execution pipeline of scien-
tific data analysis (Scope, Variable, Function, Relation-
ship, Conclusion). This taxonomy reveals that as models
improve,earlygroundingerrorsdecreasewhilelater-stage
errors persist, making Function, Relationship, and Con-
clusion Errors the dominant failure modes for stronger
models, a diagnostic signal invisible to aggregate accu-
racy scores.

LLMs,weanalyzetheirperformanceacrosssixscientifictask
types and five scientific domains.
Overall performance.Table 2 reports overall results on
theheld-outSDA-SynthtestsplitunderbothOEQandMCQ
formats. Because the four-option MCQ format has a 25%
chance floor, OEQ and MCQ accuracies are not directly
comparable; we use OEQ as the primary metric and treat
MCQ as a complementary signal.
Closed-source models set the strongest range, with GPT-
5.4 at 58.33%, Gemini 3.1 Pro at 56.88%, and Claude Son-
net 4.6 at 55.79% OEQ accuracy. Fine-tuned Llama-3.1-
8B-Instruct approaches this range under both formats; the
error-type objective further raises OEQ to 55.33%, suggest-
ing task-aligned supervision helps smaller models learn the
benchmark's analysis structure.
Comparing the two formats reveals divergent behaviors.

Error Analysis Framework.Aggregate accuracy cannot
reveal where in the analysis execution process a model fails.
We therefore conducted a bottom-up inspection of incorrect
responsesandidentifiedfiverecurringfailuremodesordered
along the execution of scientific data analysis: (1) Scope Er-
ror, misinterpreting the analytical target or task scope; (2)
Variable Error, selecting the wrong analysis variables; (3)
Function Error, choosing or applying an incorrect analyt-
ical method; (4) Relationship Error, mischaracterizing the
existence, direction, strength, or structure of variable inter-
actions; and (5) Conclusion Error, drawing a final inference
unsupported by the preceding analysis. We annotate the first

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding model performance drop-offs on mechanistic and exploratory tasks relative to basic descriptive tasks, as well as the persistence of later-stage reasoning errors over variable-grounding errors in stronger models, are directly aligned with the empirical findings.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation covers 15 open and proprietary LLMs under zero-shot and fine-tuned settings across held-out synthetic test splits and real-world datasets, supplemented by a fine-grained five-stage failure categorization (Scope, Variable, Function, Relationship, Conclusion) with normalized error rates.
primary.limitations: The authors explicitly discuss constraints including the potential gap between synthetic semantic graph dynamics and real experimental confounders, the risk of MCQ options inducing superficial heuristics, and annotating only the first execution error.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is clearly defined, utilizing semantic directed acyclic graphs and internally standardized structural causal models for synthetic generation, paired with an automated four-agent template construction and deterministic programmatic derivation pipeline to establish verifiable ground truth.
primary.quality_rationale: The benchmark provides a well-substantiated, methodologically sound framework addressing known pitfalls in execution-only LLM evaluations. Data generation, programmatic verification, and diagnostic error evaluations are thoroughly documented and scientifically credible.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces SDABench, an evaluation benchmark for scientific data analysis across six reasoning capabilities and five scientific domains, comprising 527 real-data instances and 6,000 synthetic instances evaluated under both open-ended and multiple-choice formats alongside a five-stage error analysis framework.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The benchmark provides a well-substantiated, methodologically sound framework addressing known pitfalls in execution-only LLM evaluations. Data generation, programmatic verification, and diagnostic error evaluations are thoroughly documented and scientifically credible.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly discuss constraints including the potential gap between synthetic semantic graph dynamics and real experimental confounders, the risk of MCQ options inducing superficial heuristics, and annotating only the first execution error.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
